title: UK culture
subtitle: Bonfire Night, fish and chips, a state school
summary: Learn the special days, the traditional food, the schools and the politics of the UK.

lesson.heading: Special days
rows: send Christmas cards, give presents, spend time with their families, decorate a Christmas tree, eat a lot
sing and dance, toast the New Year
send cards to a boyfriend / girlfriend / husband / wife
children dress up and knock at doors to ask for sweets
lesson.note: A **bank holiday** is a day when most organisations are closed.

lesson.heading: Food
lesson.text: Traditional UK food is **fish and chips**, and **roast beef** with **roast potatoes** [cooked in the oven] and **Yorkshire pudding** [a dish made of flour, milk and eggs].

examples.text: We had **fish and chips** by the sea.
On Sunday we eat **roast beef** with **roast potatoes** and **Yorkshire pudding**.
examples.note: The Yorkshire pudding comes with the main course, not after it.

examples.text: **Chicken tikka masala** comes from India, but it is very popular in the UK.
examples.note: It is a kind of curry.

lesson.heading: Education
rows: parents don't pay for children to go here
parents pay for children to go here
lesson.note: You can put the words together: *a state primary school*, *a private secondary school*.

lesson.heading: Politics
lesson.text: The UK has a **royal family**, with a **king** or a **queen**. Political decisions are made at the **Houses of Parliament**, and the **Prime Minister** is the political leader of the country.

examples.text: Political decisions are made at the **Houses of Parliament**.
The **Prime Minister** is the political leader of the UK.

lesson.text: Learn the special days with their dates together - *Bonfire Night, 5th November* - so you remember both at the same time.

exercises.explanation: Halloween is on 31st October. Children dress up and ask for sweets.

exercises.prompt: Match each festival with what people do.

pairs.right: decorate a tree and give presents
children dress up and ask for sweets
send cards to a boyfriend or girlfriend
sing and dance, and toast the New Year

exercises.prompt: New Year's Day is a ___ holiday - most organisations are closed.
exercises.explanation: A bank holiday is a day when most organisations are closed.

exercises.prompt: British people traditionally eat fish with ___.
exercises.explanation: Fish and chips is traditional UK food.

exercises.prompt: Chicken tikka masala is popular in the UK, but it comes from ___.
exercises.explanation: Chicken tikka masala comes from India.

exercises.prompt: Chicken tikka masala is a kind of ...
exercises.explanation: Chicken tikka masala is a kind of curry.

exercises.statement: British people eat Yorkshire pudding after their main course.
exercises.explanation: No. They eat it with their main course, with roast beef.

exercises.prompt: You make roast beef and roast potatoes in the ___.
exercises.explanation: Roast food is cooked in the oven.

exercises.prompt: Which kind of school does each child go to?
Gabriel is 14. His school is free. What kind of school does he go to?
exercises.explanation: Free = a state school. Aged 12-18 = a secondary school.

exercises.statement: Parents pay for their children to go to a state school.
exercises.explanation: Parents don't pay for a state school. They pay for a private school.

exercises.prompt: Political decisions in the UK are made at the Houses of ___.
exercises.explanation: The Prime Minister works at the Houses of Parliament.

exercises.answer: The Prime Minister is the political leader of the UK.
exercises.explanation: The Prime Minister is the political leader; the king or queen is the head of the royal family.
